Backups & restore

A backup is a copy of the panel's database: users, nodes, settings, secrets and the audit log.

Treat a backup as secret material

The database holds node API keys and the owner password hash. It is encrypted at rest with AES-256-GCM using a key in the data directory (mode 0600), and the data directory itself is 0700. Move any off-site copy over an encrypted channel.

Take a backup now

Backups land in /var/lib/ovmanager/backups, and the newest 14 are kept unless you change that. Each backup is a plain .db file named ovmanager-<label>-<stamp>.db, written 0600: a consistent SQLite snapshot taken through the online-backup API — safe while the panel is writing — staged in a temporary file and only then published under its final name. Older copies are pruned as they are made.

Restores stage and verify the candidate (PRAGMA quick_check and a schema check) before it replaces anything, so a truncated or edited backup is refused rather than overwriting your live data.

A daily backup

The installer writes a systemd timer ovmanager-backup.timer that runs ovmanager backup --keep 7 daily, whether or not the panel is up. The panel's own scheduler does not supplement it — the timer is the schedule; pick no more than one.

Off-site copies

For an off-site copy, the installer can push the newest backup to another machine after each backup (the daily timer and any manual ovmanager backup). Fill in a target like backup@server:/backups/panel and, after each run, the newest file is copied there with rsync (or scp when rsync is not installed).

  • The transfer uses plain SSH with key-based login and BatchMode — no password prompts.
  • The target machine must already accept your key, and the target folder must already exist.
  • Success or failure is written to the audit log. Nothing else on the remote side is created, rotated or cleaned up — retention is yours to manage there.

Restoring

From the CLI

ovmanager restore with no name lists what is available and changes nothing. Naming a backup restores it, with the service stopped and restarted around the swap.

From the panel

The panel's Backup & restore page accepts an uploaded backup and restores it atomically:

  • Writes are refused until the swap has finished, so nothing is half-written against a database being replaced.
  • The database being replaced is kept as a fallback.
  • The restored database is migrated on the spot, so an older backup comes back at the current schema version.

What is in a backup, and what is not

ItemBacked up by ovmanager backup
Users, expiry, quotas, tags, admin accountsYes — in the database
Nodes, their API keys and device limitsYes — in the database
Settings and the audit logYes — in the database
Panel TLS key and certificateNo — they live outside the database
VPN user profiles and node stateNo — those live on each node

A complete disaster-recovery plan has two halves: the panel database here, and each node's state. Back both up.
